# Synkopa

> Synkopa is a free, open-source digital audio workstation (DAW) for Windows, macOS and Linux. It works the FL Studio way (patterns, Channel Rack, piano roll, playlist), includes audio recording and vocal pitch editing, and installs a `synkopa` command line through which a script or an AI agent can edit the project that is open in the app.

Facts, as of version 0.9 (November 2026):

- Price: free. One build, no paid edition, no account.
- Licence: AGPL-3.0-only.
- Platforms: Windows (WASAPI, ASIO) and Linux (ALSA and JACK, including PipeWire's JACK; deb, rpm, AppImage) and macOS 13.4+ on Apple Silicon (Core Audio; .dmg, not notarized; no VST3 hosting yet).
- Engine: Rust; the audio callback does not allocate, lock or do I/O. Interface: Tauri 2, SolidJS, canvas.
- Built in: a wavetable synth, a sampled grand piano (Synkopa Keys), a sampler with a drum and tonal library, and 16 effects (dynamic EQ, compressor, FET compressor, saturator, delay, reverb, limiter, de-esser, denoiser, pitch correction, voice, vocal rider, halftime, warp, chorus, phaser).
- Performance (measured 16 Nov 2026 against FL Studio 20.7.2 on the same PC, songs of matched size, medians): opening a large song 0.44 s vs 10.57 s, opening the piano roll 39 ms vs 639 ms, adding an effect and opening its window 59 ms vs 575 ms, startup 1.32 s vs 1.64 s, clip drag 17 ms vs 16 ms (FL slightly ahead), no audio dropouts in either during 10 minutes of editing. Method: https://github.com/miskibin/synkopa/blob/main/perf/realworld/README.md
- Recording: loop recording with takes and comping, measured latency compensation, live monitoring.
- Vocals: note-level pitch editor, live pitch correction, Tune to Reference, vocal rider.
- Third-party plugins: VST3 instruments and effects on Windows and Linux, plus LV2 effects on Linux. Compatible native editors work on both platforms, otherwise Synkopa shows parameters. Plugin scanning runs out of process; plugin processing is not sandboxed. No CLAP or LV2 instruments.
- Not available: Session view or clip launching, FL Studio project (.flp) import.
- Mixing: insert buses and sends, flexible mixer docking, effect-chain presets and plugin delay compensation.
- MIDI: keyboard note input and recording, import and export of standard MIDI files.
- Export: mixes and stems to 16-/24-bit PCM or 32-bit float WAV or MP3; portable project ZIP export.
- Development: an open-source project with community contributors and AI-assisted coding. Special thanks to [@rebizu](https://github.com/rebizu) for architecture, test and Piano Roll contributions. See the [contributors](https://github.com/miskibin/synkopa/graphs/contributors).

## Product philosophy

The rules that decide which features, built-in plugins, factory content and pull requests get in:

- Curated over comprehensive: one great stock EQ or reverb beats five mediocre ones. Every built-in plugin, preset and sample must have a distinct musical role and pass a listening test; filler is improved or cut.
- Shared project context, backed by DSP: built-in tools use the tempo, key, track routing and audio signal the DAW already knows (tempo matching, scale guides, vocal tuning key, DSP-based mix checks), always with A/B preview and one-click dismissal. AI automation lives in the CLI and external agents, not in a chat sidebar.
- Automate the housekeeping: track naming, colouring, mixer routing and crash-safe autosave should need no manual setup. Unnecessary dialogs, window switches and lost sessions are treated as bugs.
- Built to finish songs: recording, comping, vocal tuning, mixing and mastering belong in the same app as pattern-based beatmaking, so a track goes from loop to export without switching DAWs.
- One UI language: built-in plugins share layout rules, controls, shortcuts and metering; visuals show what the audio is doing (curves and meters over skeuomorphic knobs).
- Local-first and open: free, open-source, offline by default, scriptable via CLI. No accounts, no subscriptions, no paywalled core features.
- Non-goals before 1.0: duplicate synths or effects, built-in AI song generators, in-app chatbots, DJ modes, feature-checklist parity with legacy DAWs.
